item.research_question: How can the pore structure of rare-earth-zirconate high-entropy ceramics be regulated to achieve low thermal conductivity and high compressive strength for thermal insulation applications?
item.processing_route: Tert-butyl alcohol (TBA)-based gel-casting method; initial solid loadings of 5–15 vol%; sintering at 1500 °C for 2 h after debinding at 620 °C for 1 h
item.test_conditions: Room temperature to 1200 °C; compressive strength testing at 0.5 mm/min crosshead speed; porosity via Archimedes' method; thermal conductivity via laser method (LFA-1000)
key_findings: Porous high-entropy ceramics exhibited a single fluorite phase without impurity phases.
Porosity ranged from 67.1% to 81.5% as solid loading increased from 15 vol% to 5 vol%.
Compressive strength increased from 1.02 ± 0.61 MPa to 6.45 ± 1.76 MPa with increasing solid loading.
Room temperature thermal conductivity ranged from 0.0642 to 0.1213 W/(m·K).
The sample with 81.5% porosity showed a thermal conductivity of 0.1467 W/(m·K) at 1200 °C.
Average pore size decreased from 1.63 μm to 1.19 μm as solid loading increased from 5 vol% to 10 vol%.
Grain size was approximately 1 μm with uniform and irregular pore opening structures.
item.mechanism: The unique pore structure with micron size (1–2 μm) impedes heat propagation by scattering electromagnetic waves corresponding to the peak of radiant heat transfer (1.6–2.9 μm) according to Mie scattering law, while high porosity reduces convective and conductive heat transfer through air-filled pores.
item.limitations: The experimental results do not completely fit the Effective Medium Theory (EMT) model, likely due to uneven distribution of pore size; the Maxwell–Eucken equation is insufficient because it lacks consideration of heat transport when phases are continuous.
item.future_work: The authors state that rare-earth-zirconate porous high-entropy ceramics with tailored pore structures are expected to be thermal insulation materials, implying further development of tailored structures for high-temperature applications.
quotes: The regulation of pore structures was realized through changing different initial solid loadings.
The unique pore structure with a micron size contributed to their excellent thermal insulating performance.
It is this unique pore structure that impedes heat propagation at high temperatures, which can reduce the radiative thermal propagation.
